title: Gluing algebraic spaces along open subfunctors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Suppose there is a set-indexed family of subfunctors [def-pc-subfunctor] $F_i\subset F$ such that each $F_i$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], each map $F_i\to F$ is representable and an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the map $\coprod_iF_i\to F$ is surjective as a sheaf map, and $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space. Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 02WR (glueing-algebraic-spaces), all five hypotheses and its representability/diagonal/gluing argument.

proof.text: First, representable functors $h_Z$ on the big fppf site are sheaves. Indeed, for any fppf covering and any affine open $A$ in its target, [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] supplies finitely many affine opens of the covering schemes above $A$ whose images cover $A$. Thus the covering satisfies exactly [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to descend compatible maps into $Z$. For maps over $S$, the descended map is over $S$ because its composite to $S$ agrees with the prescribed structural map after the covering, and the uniqueness assertion of the same descent lemma detects this equality. This works for the empty target as well.

Put $H=\coprod_iF_i$ in sheaves and let $P(T)=\coprod_iF_i(T)$ be the sectionwise presheaf coproduct. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies $P^\#$ with $H$: a map from either to a sheaf $K$ is exactly a family of maps $F_i\to K$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] says that a section of $H$ is fppf locally represented by a section of one $F_i$, and equality of two such representatives in $H$ holds locally already in $P$. In particular unequal indices can coincide only on the empty scheme: every nonempty scheme admits no empty fppf covering, and restriction in $P$ preserves the index.

source.place: Tag 00WI, lemma-colimit-sheaves, universal property; Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification

proof.text: Fix a scheme $T$ and a map $h_T\to F$. By the representable-open hypothesis, $h_T\times_FF_i=h_{V_i}$ for an open subscheme $V_i\subseteq T$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. The sheaf surjectivity of $H\to F$ gives fppf local lifts of this map to $H$; refining by Step 2 gives an fppf covering $T_a\to T$ whose maps to $F$ factor through some $F_{i(a)}$. Each $T_a\to T$ therefore factors through $V_{i(a)}$ by the fibre-product universal property. The family $T_a\to T$ is jointly surjective by [def-pc-fppf-site], so $T=\bigcup_iV_i$. All such tests, including their further pullbacks, give open coverings in this way.

Let $E_T=H\times_Fh_T$. It is a sheaf: matching sections in the two factors glue uniquely, and their equality in $F$ persists by the sheaf uniqueness axiom [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Form the scheme $C_T=\coprod_iV_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Its coprojections have disjoint open images covering $C_T$. The maps $h_{V_i}\to E_T$ therefore define a natural map $h_{C_T}\to E_T$: for $W\to C_T$, restrict to the inverse images of those disjoint opens and glue the resulting sections of $E_T$. This uses [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. Every section $(a,t)$ of $E_T(W)$ fppf locally has $a$ in one $F_i$ by Step 2; the equality over $F$ then gives a map to $V_i$, hence to $C_T$. Any two local maps inducing $(a,t)$ agree: by Step 2 their indices agree after a further fppf refinement, and with the same index their maps to $V_i$ agree because $F_i\to F$ is a subfunctor and $V_i$ is its pullback to $T$. The sheaf property of $h_{C_T}$ from Step 1 glues these maps uniquely. The resulting inverse is natural and proves $h_{C_T}\simeq E_T$ over $h_T$. Thus $q:H\to F$ is representable, and its scheme test is $C_T\to T$, which is surjective by Step 3.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first paragraph: representation of the pullback of the sheaf coproduct by the scheme coproduct

proof.text: For schemes $T,T'$ mapping to $F$, set $G=h_T\times_Fh_{T'}$ and $G_i=G\times_FF_i$. Write $V_i=T\times_FF_i$ and $V'_i=T'\times_FF_i$ as in Step 3. Since $F_i\subset F$ is monic, the sectionwise pullback equations give $G_i=h_{V_i}\times_{F_i}h_{V'_i}$. This is represented by a scheme because the diagonal of the algebraic space $F_i$ is representable [def-trf-algebraic-space]. For every $h_W\to G$, the pullback of $G_i\to G$ is $h_W\times_FF_i$, an open subscheme of $W$, and these opens cover $W$ by Step 3. Thus the $G_i$ are representable open subfunctors covering $G$. Moreover $G$ is a Zariski sheaf: its sections are pairs of scheme maps with equal images in the sheaf $F$, and the sheaf condition follows by componentwise gluing, Step 1 and [lem-pc-zariski-coverings-are-fppf]. Apply [lem-pc-schemes-criterion] to obtain a scheme representing $G$. An arbitrary test of $F\to F\times F$ is exactly such a pair of maps from a scheme, so this proves representability of the diagonal of $F$.

source.place: Tag 02WR, second paragraph, applying Schemes Tag 01JJ (lemma-glue-functors)

proof.text: For every test $h_T\to F$, Step 4 represents the base change of $q$ by $C_T=\coprod_iV_i\to T$. Its restriction to each coproduct summand is the open immersion $V_i\hookrightarrow T$, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). The summands are an open covering by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] to conclude that $C_T\to T$ is etale. It is surjective by Step 3. Hence $q:H\to F$ is representable, surjective and etale, in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and last paragraphs; morphisms.tex Tags 02GP and 02GJ

proof.text: By the hypothesis that $H$ is an algebraic space and [def-trf-algebraic-space], choose a scheme $U$ and a representable surjective etale map $h_U\to H$. For any $h_T\to F$, the fibre-product equations identify $h_U\times_Fh_T$ with $h_U\times_HE_T$. Step 4 represents $E_T$ by the scheme $C_T$. Therefore $h_U\times_HE_T$ is a scheme, and its projection to $C_T$ is etale and surjective by the scheme-test definition for the atlas $h_U\to H$. The map $C_T\to T$ is etale and surjective by Step 6. Their composite is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](2) and surjective by [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition]. Thus $h_U\to F$ is a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. Together with the given fppf sheaf condition and Step 5's representable diagonal, this is precisely the definition of an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 02WR, last paragraph: compose the coproduct atlas with the representable surjective etale map to F

proof_origin.place: Tag 02WR, lemma-glueing-algebraic-spaces, all three paragraphs; the composite atlas is checked on scheme tests, using etaleness of the coproduct map.

lean.statement: theorem algebraicSpace_of_open_gluing {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (I : Type w) (Fi : I → Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (j : ∀ i : I, (Fi i) ⟶ H) (hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j)) (ι : ∀ i : I, (Fi i) ⟶ F) (q : H ⟶ F) (hfac : ∀ i : I, j i ≫ q = ι i) (hmono : ∀ i : I, Mono (ι i)) (hFi : ∀ i : I, AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace (Fi i)) (hopen : ∀ i : I, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (ι i).hom) (hq : Epi q) (hcop : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace H) : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace F
lean.note: The set-indexed sheaf coproduct is represented explicitly by injections j into H together with hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j); q : H ⟶ F is the canonical coproduct map, hfac identifies its summand restrictions with the family maps, hq expresses sheaf surjectivity, and hcop expresses algebraicity of H.
